review_notes: Inspected all 93 lines, the imported torus and row-series APIs, related summability results, and downstream uses. One repeated Fourier-series argument merits sharing. Proposed replacements were not executed.

findings.problem: Lines 43–54 repeat the coefficient-recovery argument in cubicThetaTorusRemainder_coefficient: compose the coefficient map with the continuous-to-L² inclusion, commute it through a convergent Fourier series, and use orthogonality to isolate one coefficient. Both proofs depend on exactly the same analytic and basis machinery; only their scalar coefficient families differ.
findings.proposed_change:
Introduce a shared lemma after cubicThetaTorusFourier_toLp in CubicThetaEisensteinTorus.lean, under its existing measure instances:

lemma cubicThetaTorusSeries_coefficient
    (a : Eisenstein → ℂ) (ha : Summable a) (k : Eisenstein) :
    cubicThetaTorusCoefficient
      (ContinuousMap.toLp 2 volume ℂ
        (∑' h : Eisenstein, a h • cubicThetaTorusFourier h)) k = a k

Proof sketch: obtain summability in continuous maps from ha.norm using norm_smul and mFourier_norm; apply the composed coefficient map to the tsum; then use cubicThetaTorusFourier_toLp, cubicThetaTorusCoefficient_basis and tsum_eq_single. This packages convergence and orthogonality, rather than merely extracting the repeated local map.

Rewrite the target proof as:
  simpa only [cubicThetaArithmeticModelRemainder] using
    cubicThetaTorusSeries_coefficient (cubicThetaArithmeticRowTerm 0 v)
      (cubicThetaArithmeticRowTerm_summable 0 hv) k

Rewrite cubicThetaTorusRemainder_coefficient as:
  simpa only [cubicThetaTorusRemainder] using
    cubicThetaTorusSeries_coefficient (cubicThetaNonzeroFrequencyTerm (0,v) s)
      (cubicThetaNonzeroFrequencyTerm_summable (p := (0,v)) hv hs) k

Both uses retain their actual positivity/convergence hypotheses and require no new imports. The helper should allow arbitrary k, including zero, and arbitrary summable a; zero-mode exclusion remains in the particular coefficient families.
findings.benefit: Centralizes the uniform-convergence-to-coefficient argument and its normalization-sensitive orthogonality calculation. Readers of both specialized theorems then see only the relevant coefficient family and convergence hypotheses, while future Fourier API changes need updating in one proof.
